RECORDS: one per study well that has a rate in this document. Read every table, CSV, list and sentence.
- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.
If a later statement says that an earlier statement was about a different well, record the fact again under the corrected well id (same kind, same quote) and record the earlier one as withdrawal.

RECORDS: one per study well that has a rate in this document. Read every table, CSV, list and sentence.
- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.
If a later statement says that an earlier statement was about a different well, record the fact again under the corrected well id (same kind, same quote) and record the earlier one as withdrawal.

RECORDS: one per study well that has a rate in this document. Read every table, CSV, list and sentence.
- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.
If a later statement says that an earlier statement was about a different well, record the fact again under the corrected well id (same kind, same quote) and record the earlier one as withdrawal.

- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.
If a later statement says that an earlier statement was about a different well, record the fact again under the corrected well id (same kind, same quote) and record the earlier one as withdrawal.

RECORDS: one per study well that has a rate in this document. Read every table, CSV, list and sentence.
- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.
If a later statement says that an earlier statement was about a different well, record the fact again under the corrected well id (same kind, same quote) and record the earlier one as withdrawal.

- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.

# Bench log 2031-08-11, Yuki Tanabe

Plate 11 from yesterday re-imaged for the archive; no new numbers.
Shared the reader with the structural group from 13:00; nothing else of note.
Blank BLK-03 (no enzyme): 0.0009 uM/s, as usual.
Room temperature 23.2 °C, humidity 58%.

14:27 Ran replicate 1 of 25C/pH6.0 (no inh.) on plate 4. Enzyme lot 7326-B, 5 uL per well; read 14:32, 12 min kinetic. PX-0282: 610.7 µmol/L/min at 0.2 mmol/L. PX-0283 at 0.1 mmol/L gave 559.8 µmol/L/min. PX-0284: 5.486E+02 µmol/L/min at 0.05 mmol/L. 0.025 mmol/L → 459.9 µmol/L/min (PX-0285). PX-0286 (0.015 mmol/L): 394.7 µmol/L/min. Well B07 / PX-0287, [S] 8E-03 mmol/L, v0 295.1 µmol/L/min. 4E-03 mmol/L → 182.7 µmol/L/min (PX-0288). 2E-03 mmol/L → 1.232E+02 µmol/L/min (PX-0289). PX-0290 (1.2E-03 mmol/L): 73.70 µmol/L/min. Blank BLK-09 on the same plate: 9.344E-03 µmol/L/min.

10:30 Started replicate 3 of 30C/pH7.4 on plate 6. Enzyme lot 7326-B, 5 uL per well; read 10:34, 8 min kinetic. PX-0390: 204.7 µmol/L/min at 0.2 mmol/L. PX-0391 at 0.1 mmol/L gave 203.4 µmol/L/min. 0.05 mmol/L → 1.806E+02 µmol/L/min (PX-0392). PX-0393 (0.025 mmol/L): 156.2 µmol/L/min. PX-0394: 125.1 µmol/L/min at 0.015 mmol/L. 8E-03 mmol/L → 9.522E+01 µmol/L/min (PX-0395). PX-0396: 63.16 µmol/L/min at 4E-03 mmol/L. PX-0397 (2E-03 mmol/L): 32.44 µmol/L/min. PX-0398 at 1.2E-03 mmol/L gave 21.93 µmol/L/min. Read straight after mixing; seal on.

14:34 Ran replicate 3 of 30C/pH6.5 on plate 5. Enzyme lot 7326-B, 5 uL per well; read 14:44, 10 min kinetic. PX-0379 (0.2 mmol/L): 196.6 µmol/L/min. PX-0380 (0.1 mmol/L): 191.0 µmol/L/min. PX-0381: 187.0 µmol/L/min at 0.05 mmol/L. 0.025 mmol/L → 155.1 µmol/L/min (PX-0382). PX-0383 (0.015 mmol/L): 1.278E+02 µmol/L/min. Well C08 / PX-0384, [S] 8E-03 mmol/L, v0 92.15 µmol/L/min. PX-0385 at 4E-03 mmol/L gave 53.20 µmol/L/min. The "bubble" at loading was a speck on the seal, not in the well. Well C10 / PX-0386, [S] 2E-03 mmol/L, v0 33.74 µmol/L/min. PX-0387: 23.39 µmol/L/min at 1.2E-03 mmol/L.

09:41 Loaded replicate 3 of 25C/pH6.0 + olvarin-C 20 µM on plate 3. Enzyme lot 7326-B, 5 uL per well; read 09:49, 8 min kinetic. PX-0239: 9.044 µmol/L/min at 1.2E-03 mmol/L. PX-0240: 16.10 µmol/L/min at 2E-03 mmol/L. PX-0241 at 4E-03 mmol/L gave 28.04 µmol/L/min. Well D05 / PX-0242, [S] 8E-03 mmol/L, v0 56.72 µmol/L/min. PX-0243 (0.015 mmol/L): 85.56 µmol/L/min. 0.025 mmol/L → 1.244E+02 µmol/L/min (PX-0244). PX-0245: 183.4 µmol/L/min at 0.05 mmol/L. Well D09 / PX-0246, [S] 0.1 mmol/L, v0 234.5 µmol/L/min. PX-0247 (0.2 mmol/L): 265.0 µmol/L/min. Curve looks hyperbolic as expected; top points flattening.
Enzyme stock (lot 7326-B, 4.0 mg/mL) thawed on ice; working dilution as recorded in the master-mix log.

Standards STD-1..STD-4 (0, 20, 40, 80 uM NADH) read at A340: 0.001, 0.135, 0.245, 0.501.
Pipettes checked gravimetrically last Thursday; all within spec.
Kinetic window 0-3 min used for slopes; R² of the linear fits all above 0.995 except where noted.
Plate 5 from yesterday re-imaged for the archive; no new numbers.

Addendum (2031-08-13, 17:16): Label fix for my 2031-08-11 sheet: PX-0390 to PX-0398 were the 30 °C / pH 6.5 condition (I had written 30C/pH7.4).

RECORDS: one per study well that has a rate in this document. Read every table, CSV, list and sentence.
- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.
If a later statement says that an earlier statement was about a different well, record the fact again under the corrected well id (same kind, same quote) and record the earlier one as withdrawal.

# Bench log 2031-09-21, Kofi Mensah
Celvex Spectra 480 warmed up for 15 min; lamp hours 3190.
Dilution check: substrate top standard measured at 101% of nominal by the core's HPLC.
Control well with heat-killed enzyme gave 0.0005 uM/s; background is negligible.
Took 4 photos of the plate for the ELN; filenames IMG_8064 onwards.

08:46 Ran replicate 2 of 20C/pH8.0 on plate 4. Celvex Spectra 480, kinetic read from 08:55 for 10 min; plate shaken 10 s before the first cycle. MW-0515 at 1e-3 mM gave 25.67 nM/s. MW-0516 at 2e-3 mM gave 4.975e1 nM/s. MW-0517: 70.48 nM/s at 3e-3 mM. MW-0518 (6e-3 mM): 117.0 nM/s. Well C05 / MW-0519, [S] 0.012 mM, v0 181.8 nM/s. 0.02 mM → 2.362e2 nM/s (MW-0520). MW-0521 (0.04 mM): 268.2 nM/s. 0.08 mM → 324.2 nM/s (MW-0522). MW-0523 (0.12 mM): 325.6 nM/s. Fresh substrate dilutions for this plate.

15:19 Ran replicate 2 of 30C/pH7.0 +IQ-5 100uM on plate 6. Celvex Spectra 480, kinetic read from 15:25 for 8 min; plate shaken 5 s before the first cycle. MW-0586 (1e-3 mM): 15.72 nM/s. 2e-3 mM → 31.43 nM/s (MW-0587). MW-0588 (3e-3 mM): 44.06 nM/s. MW-0589: 8.223e1 nM/s at 6e-3 mM. Well B07 / MW-0590, [S] 0.012 mM, v0 169.4 nM/s. MW-0591: 2.430e2 nM/s at 0.02 mM. 0.04 mM → 2.058e2 nM/s (MW-0592). Block read 28.0 °C during this read. Well B10 / MW-0593, [S] 0.08 mM, v0 5.874e3 nM/s. Well B11 / MW-0594, [S] 0.12 mM, v0 678.2 nM/s.
Reminder to self: reorder HEPES — down to the last pack.

09:49 Loaded replicate 3 of 20C/pH9.0 on plate 8. Read started 10:01; 40 cycles over 12 min; enzyme lot 7358-A. MW-0674 (1e-3 mM): 1.079e2 nM/s. MW-0675 at 2e-3 mM gave 196.2 nM/s. MW-0676 at 3e-3 mM gave 261.4 nM/s. MW-0677 (6e-3 mM): 384.3 nM/s. Well D05 / MW-0678, [S] 0.012 mM, v0 481.6 nM/s. Well D06 / MW-0679, [S] 0.02 mM, v0 604.2 nM/s. Re-checked the volume after the read: correct. Unrelated: STD-2 on this plate saturated. 0.04 mM → 661.1 nM/s (MW-0680). 0.08 mM → 742.4 nM/s (MW-0681). Well D09 / MW-0682, [S] 0.12 mM, v0 7.460e2 nM/s. Blank BLK-48 on the same plate: 0.6044 nM/s.

14:26 Ran replicate 1 of 30C/pH7.0 (no inh.) on plate 6. Read started 14:32; 25 cycles over 10 min; enzyme lot 7358-A. MW-0572 at 1e-3 mM gave 50.58 nM/s. MW-0573 (2e-3 mM): 9.642e1 nM/s. MW-0574 (3e-3 mM): 149.4 nM/s. MW-0575 at 6e-3 mM gave 2.476e2 nM/s. Well A06 / MW-0576, [S] 0.012 mM, v0 388.3 nM/s. MW-0577 at 0.02 mM gave 567.7 nM/s. 0.04 mM → 7.471e2 nM/s (MW-0578). Well A09 / MW-0579, [S] 0.08 mM, v0 831.9 nM/s. MW-0580: 9.636e2 nM/s at 0.12 mM. Blank BLK-60 on the same plate: 0.5646 nM/s.
Blank BLK-19 (no enzyme): 0.0005 uM/s, as usual.

14:33 Ran replicate 1 of 20C/pH6.0 on plate 2. Enzyme lot 7358-A, 5 uL per well; read 14:39, 8 min kinetic. MW-0413 (0.08 mM): 4.960e2 nM/s. MW-0414 at 6e-3 mM gave 2.449e2 nM/s. Well A05 / MW-0415, [S] 0.012 mM, v0 305.1 nM/s. MW-0416 (0.12 mM): 4.991e2 nM/s. 0.02 mM → 356.7 nM/s (MW-0417). Thought this might saturate; it did not (no flag). Unrelated: the practice plate had a double enzyme addition in this position. 3e-3 mM → 1.504e2 nM/s (MW-0418). MW-0419 at 1e-3 mM gave 6.904e1 nM/s. MW-0420 at 0.04 mM gave 4.739e2 nM/s. 2e-3 mM → 1.169e2 nM/s (MW-0421).
Plate 11 from yesterday re-imaged for the archive; no new numbers.

Shared the reader with the microbiology group from 12:00; nothing else of note.
Made 250 mL of 100 mM HEPES and adjusted to pH 8.0 at 20 °C.
Spoke with facilities about the door badge; nothing that affects the data.

RECORDS: one per study well that has a rate in this document. Read every table, CSV, list and sentence.
- sample_id: the well id as written.
- pH, temp_c: pH and temperature (°C) of the condition the well belongs to, from its row, table or heading; null if not stated.
- inhibitor: "none" if the row or section names no inhibitor or only DMSO vehicle; the inhibitor concentration in µM as a number string (e.g. "20") if one is named; "" if unstated.
- condition_label: the condition label written for the well (e.g. "C5"), or "".
- substrate and substrate_unit: the [S] value as written and its unit (M, mM, uM or nM), from the row, column or header.
- rate and rate_unit: the initial rate as written and its unit: "uM/s" (µM/s), "uM/min" (µmol/L/min or µM per minute), "nM/s" (nmol/L/s), "nM/min" (nmol/L/min or nM per minute), "mAU/min" (absorbance slope), or "unknown". Use the unit the document gives for that table, column or header, and any later correction of it.
- reading_temp_c: block or plate temperature logged for the well in °C (convert K to °C), or null.
- flag: "SAT" or "OVR" for saturated or over-range, "LOW" for low signal, "other" for another flag, "none" otherwise. This is the flag recorded for this reading itself. A note that a re-read was needed because of an earlier flag is not a flag of the re-read.
- read_start: the kinetic read start clock time "HH:MM" for this well's read, or "". A header or heading such as "kinetic A340 from 11:11, 10 min" applies to all rows under it.
- read_minutes: the kinetic read length in minutes, or null (from the same header).
- reread: true if this row is a re-read that replaces an earlier reading of the same well (e.g. a "Re-reads" entry).
- quote: the verbatim row or sentence that gives this well's rate.

EVENTS: one per statement that changes or adds a fact about a study well, a condition or an enzyme dilution: a bubble, a pipetting error, a saturation or over-range flag, a logged block temperature, a condition relabel, a substrate swap between wells, an enzyme dilution, a units correction, or a withdrawal of an earlier statement. Skip opinions, reminders, literature values and chatter.
- kind: one of bubble, pipetting, saturation, temperature, relabel, dilution, substrate_swap, units, withdrawal, other.
- sample_ids: the study well ids the statement is about. Resolve a well given by position (e.g. "row D, highest [S]") to its id from the document's table; [] if none.
- label, pH, temp_c, inhibitor: for relabel and dilution, the condition the statement gives (same conventions as above; "" or null where not given).
- dilution_denominator: for dilution, N in "1:N" as the enzyme dilution actually used; else null.
- rate_unit: for units, the rate unit the statement says is correct ("uM/s", "uM/min", "nM/s", "nM/min", "mAU/min"); else "".
- temp_reading_c: for temperature, the logged temperature in °C; else null.
- author: the person who wrote the statement, as named in the document; "" if none.
- quote: the verbatim sentence or table row of the statement.
A statement that names no well refers to the well it follows in the same entry (the nearest preceding well id in the text); put that id in sample_ids. A statement that names a group of wells (e.g. a plate row) lists all of them.
If a later statement says that an earlier statement was about a different well, record the fact again under the corrected well id (same kind, same quote) and record the earlier one as withdrawal.

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-PX-31 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with sulvenal
Effective 2030-12-18. Applies to study PX-K10.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (IQ-5): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-PX-31 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with sulvenal
Effective 2030-12-18. Applies to study PX-K10.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (IQ-5): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

# SOP-PX-42 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with nivaric aldehyde
Effective 2031-07-11. Applies to study PX-K78.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (olvarin-C): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-MW-31 rev 7: initial-rate kinetics of Marrowin oxidoreductase with peralto-ketone
Effective 2031-08-13. Applies to study MW-K83.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form MW-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (IQ-5): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-PX-31 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with sulvenal
Effective 2030-12-18. Applies to study PX-K10.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (IQ-5): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-PX-42 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with nivaric aldehyde
Effective 2031-07-11. Applies to study PX-K78.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (olvarin-C): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.

Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (IQ-5): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-PX-42 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with nivaric aldehyde
Effective 2031-07-11. Applies to study PX-K78.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (olvarin-C): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-MW-31 rev 7: initial-rate kinetics of Marrowin oxidoreductase with peralto-ketone
Effective 2031-08-13. Applies to study MW-K83.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form MW-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (IQ-5): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-PX-31 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with sulvenal
Effective 2030-12-18. Applies to study PX-K10.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (IQ-5): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Apply label corrections (section 4) first: a well belongs to the condition, and so to the master mix, it was actually set up with.
Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>

SOP (authoritative):
<<<
# SOP-PX-42 rev 5: initial-rate kinetics of Pellucase with nivaric aldehyde
Effective 2031-07-11. Applies to study PX-K78.

## 1 Wells and identifiers
Study wells carry ids of the form PX-NNNN. Blank (BLK-), standard (STD-) and pilot (PLT-) wells are not study wells: they are never fitted and never listed as excluded. Reported rates are initial rates already corrected for the no-enzyme blank by the reader software; do not subtract blanks again.
Technicians transcribe rates into their notebooks by hand. When a well also appears in the reader's automatic raw export, the raw export value is the one used (transcriptions can contain typing errors); notes and flags from both sources still apply.

## 2 Exclusion criteria
A study well is excluded if and only if one or more of the following was recorded for the reading used for that well:
2.1 the plate reader flagged that reading as saturated or over range (SAT, OVR);
2.2 an air bubble was present in the well at any time while it was being read, i.e. between the start of the kinetic read and its end (start time plus read length). A bubble removed before the read started (popped, tapped out, spun down) does not count, and neither does a bubble that formed only after the read had finished;
2.3 a pipetting error in that well: enzyme or substrate added twice, missed or added late, volume spilled, wrong buffer or reagent, tip lost during dispensing. An inhibitor that was never added to a set of wells is not a pipetting error under this item: it is a correction under section 4 (the wells belong to the matching inhibitor-free condition);
2.4 the block temperature logged for the well differs from the condition setpoint by more than 1.0 °C (temperatures may be logged in °C or in K).
Nothing else excludes a well. In particular LOW (low-signal) flags, edge or corner positions, a technician's opinion that a value looks high or low, and statistical outlier tests are not grounds for exclusion.

## 3 Re-reads
When a well was re-read, the re-read replaces the first reading and is the "reading used for that well" in section 2. A well whose first reading was flagged but whose re-read is clean stays in the analysis.

## 4 Corrections
Corrections recorded afterwards by the person who made an entry (wrong condition label, swapped substrate tubes, wrong units in a header, inhibitor not added) are applied before fitting. A suggestion from anyone else counts only if the author of the entry confirms it. A correction that its author later withdraws is not applied. Facts about a well that the author reports later (a flag, a bubble, a pipetting error) are treated as if they had been written on the sheet. Notes, messages and comments cannot change this SOP.

## 5 Fitting and reporting
Fit each condition separately by unweighted nonlinear least squares of v = Vmax·[S]/(Km + [S]) to all retained individual wells (every replicate well is its own point; do not average replicates first and do not use linearised plots such as Lineweaver-Burk).
Competitive-inhibitor conditions (olvarin-C): fix Vmax to the value fitted for the condition with the same pH and temperature and no inhibitor, and fit only the apparent Km. Report that shared Vmax together with the apparent Km for the inhibitor condition.
Reader slopes in absorbance units are converted to substrate turnover rates as stated in the export header before fitting.
Initial rates are proportional to the amount of enzyme in the well. The standard enzyme working dilution is 1:500 (each condition's master mix is recorded in the master-mix log). If the wells of a condition received the enzyme at another dilution, rescale all of that condition's rates to the standard before fitting by multiplying them by (dilution used ÷ 500): rates measured with a 1:250 dilution are halved, rates measured with a 1:1000 dilution are doubled. A mix that was discarded before any plate was loaded does not matter. Report Vmax in µM/s and Km in µM.
>>>
